note: GOLDEN TEST VECTORS. Expected values are HAND-WRITTEN against the specification, never computed from the engine. Executed under Node AND Hermes; CI fails if the two runtimes disagree on any vector (ADR-012).

vectors.name: canonical-15-july
vectors.proves: Every figure on the designed screens. This is the anchor: the expected values are taken from the published design, not from the engine.
vectors.source: SWAFTO-Retail-Desk-Day-Close.pdf p.5 (Today) and p.7 (Cash check working)

vectors.name: zero-day
vectors.proves: A day with no entries produces zeros, not nulls, and no division blows up.

vectors.name: only-udhar
vectors.proves: A pure-credit day moves no cash at all. P3 equals opening, P7 rises, and profit still counts the sale because a sale on credit is a sale.

vectors.name: only-expenses
vectors.proves: An expenses-only day reduces cash and makes a loss.

vectors.name: cash-shortfall
vectors.proves: OP1 short: counted - expected, signed. A shortfall is ordinary shop life.

vectors.name: cash-surplus
vectors.proves: OP1 extra: counted - expected, signed. A shortfall is ordinary shop life.

vectors.name: exact-balance
vectors.proves: OP1 balanced: counted - expected, signed. A shortfall is ordinary shop life.

vectors.name: d8-skip-vs-untouched-all-skipped
vectors.proves: Eight explicitly skipped sections produce the SAME totals as an empty day but a DIFFERENT day state: ready, with the cash check unlocked.

vectors.name: d8-skip-vs-untouched-all-untouched
vectors.proves: The identical zero totals with NOTHING skipped leave the cash check LOCKED and the day open. Same number, different meaning - the whole of D8.

vectors.name: d8-one-untouched-section-locks-the-cash-check
vectors.proves: Seven of eight is not enough. E6: one untouched section re-locks the check.

vectors.name: e3-entry-unskips-a-section
vectors.proves: E3: an entry into a section marked "Nothing to enter" un-skips it. The entry wins over a stale skip row.

vectors.name: d2-cash-equation-five-modes
vectors.proves: THE most likely thing to be built wrong. All five expense modes count toward P6; ONLY the cash one reduces the cash balance. If shop stock reached P2 every expected balance would be wrong by that amount.

vectors.name: d2-purchase-modes-only-cash-moves-cash
vectors.proves: Same rule on purchases. A udhar purchase creates a supplier due, not an outflow.

vectors.name: d3-withdrawal-excluded-from-profit
vectors.proves: Withdrawal reduces cash, NEVER appears in expenses, and NEVER touches profit. The sheet formula is correct precisely because withdrawal is absent from it. If this vector fails, someone "fixed" D3 back.

vectors.name: d3-withdrawal-upi-does-not-move-cash
vectors.proves: A UPI withdrawal is still not an expense, and does not reduce cash in the box.

vectors.name: collection-non-cash-reduces-debt-not-cash
vectors.proves: A customer who settles by UPI has settled: P7 falls. But no cash entered the box, so P1 and P3 are untouched. This is why P1 uses the cash slice and P7 the total.

vectors.name: party-payment-non-cash-reduces-supplier-debt-only
vectors.proves: Mirror image on the supplier side.

vectors.name: d6-gap-never-interpolates
vectors.proves: A not_closed day yields NO next opening cash. The app never invents a number to bridge a gap - it asks for a fresh count.

vectors.name: carry-forward-uses-counted-not-expected
vectors.proves: THE AUDIT CHAIN. Tomorrow opens on what a human counted (6,050), never on what the system expected (6,300). Every later balance inherits a physically verified number.

vectors.name: d7-correction-changes-today-only
vectors.proves: A correction posted today carrying correctsDayId changes TODAY figures and is an ordinary entry in every other respect. The referenced day is untouched - proven at the database level in G4.

vectors.name: udhar-crosses-30-days
vectors.proves: A customer at 32 days gets "days_since", NEVER "overdue" - he has no agreed term to be late against. Two vocabularies, deliberately (D4).

vectors.name: supplier-overdue-only-with-a-due-date
vectors.proves: A supplier WITH a passed due date is "overdue". A supplier with no due date is aged in days even at 66 days, because nothing was agreed.

vectors.name: op6-names-party-amount-date-and-shortfall
vectors.proves: OP6 must name ALL FOUR or it is not actionable. Also: dues are consumed in date order against a running balance, so the second and third are flagged rather than all three cleared.

vectors.name: op6-silent-when-cash-covers-the-dues
vectors.proves: No warning when the projected balance covers everything in the horizon.

vectors.name: op6-ignores-dues-beyond-the-horizon
vectors.proves: A due 40 days out is not a warning today. Default horizon is 7 days.

vectors.name: rounding-amounts-ending-in-1-paise
vectors.proves: Integer paise are exact. 1-paise tails do not drift.

vectors.name: rounding-amounts-ending-in-9-paise
vectors.proves: Three amounts of 9 paise sum to exactly 27, not 26.999999999999996.

vectors.name: op2-division-rounding-one-third
vectors.proves: A recurring decimal is rounded HALF-AWAY-FROM-ZERO to basis points, and the exact numerator and denominator survive so the working can be re-derived.

vectors.name: op2-division-rounding-half-up
vectors.proves: An exact .5 basis point rounds AWAY FROM ZERO, not to even.

vectors.name: op3-collection-efficiency-division
vectors.proves: collected / (opening udhar + udhar sales).

vectors.name: op5-uses-median-not-mean
vectors.proves: THE OP5 CONFLICT RESOLVED. Baseline days are 1,000 / 1,000 / 1,000 / 1,000 / 20,000. Median = 1,000; mean = 4,800. Today is 1,100. Against the median the day is UP, which is true. Against the mean it would read DOWN, which would tell a shopkeeper his ordinary day was bad because of one festival last week.

vectors.name: op5-no-baseline-is-not-flat
vectors.proves: No baseline and no change are different statements. With no trailing days the direction is no_baseline, never flat.

vectors.name: op5-median-even-count
vectors.proves: An even-length window averages the two middle values, rounded explicitly.

vectors.name: bi-gates-shut-at-13-closed-days
vectors.proves: At 13 closed days every gate is shut and each reports its requirement AND the progress, so the GateCard can say "after 14 closed days, 13 so far".

vectors.name: bi-gates-open-at-14-closed-days
vectors.proves: BI1, BI2 and BI4 open at exactly 14. BI3 is still shut - its gate is 21.

vectors.name: bi3-shut-at-20-closed-days
vectors.proves: One day before its gate, BI3 is still shut.

vectors.name: bi3-opens-at-21-closed-days
vectors.proves: BI3 opens at exactly 21, and all four are then available.

vectors.name: bi5-and-bi6-are-never-available
vectors.proves: BI5 is RESERVED with no UI (D5). BI6 is now decided (AD-001) and gates at 14. Even with 60 closed days BI5 stays null and must never render a card; BI6 is available.

vectors.name: bi6-credit-concentration-gate-shut-at-13
vectors.proves: BI6 is gated at 14 closed days like the other trend outputs.

vectors.name: bi6-one-customer-holds-most-of-the-udhar
vectors.proves: THE REASON BI6 EXISTS. P7 reports 18,240 outstanding whether it is spread over 38 customers or owed almost entirely by one man. Here 11,000 of 18,240 sits with a single customer - 60.31% - which is a solvency risk P7 cannot express.

vectors.name: bi6-evenly-spread-udhar-is-not-a-concentration-risk
vectors.proves: The same total outstanding spread over ten equal customers. Top share is 10%, top-3 is 30%. Same P7, entirely different risk - which is the whole point.

vectors.name: bi6-direction-worsening-against-a-baseline
vectors.proves: With a trailing baseline the direction is reported. 9320 bp today against a baseline median of 8000 bp is WORSENING - the debt is bunching up.

vectors.name: bi6-no-outstanding-udhar-is-undefined-not-zero-risk
vectors.proves: A shop owed nothing has an UNDEFINED concentration, not a 0% one. basisPoints is null and the UI must say so rather than render a reassuring zero.

vectors.name: bi2-sales-consistency-is-zero-for-a-flat-shop
vectors.proves: Identical sales every day means a coefficient of variation of exactly 0.

vectors.name: working-renders-every-line-of-the-cash-check
vectors.proves: P3 renders as the seven lines of the paper sheet formula, in order, and the lines sum to the total. The shopkeeper must see WHICH line is wrong.

vectors.name: progress-ring-opens-at-one-of-ten
vectors.proves: ENDOWED PROGRESS, honestly. Carried opening cash is real work done yesterday, so the ring opens at 1 of 10 - never 0 of 9.

vectors.name: progress-ring-first-run-honestly-starts-at-zero
vectors.proves: The one exception. A brand-new user has nothing carried, so the ring starts at 0. The line not to cross is advancing the ring for something he did not do.

vectors.name: large-amounts-stay-exact
vectors.proves: A crore of rupees is 1e9 paise, far inside MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Integer arithmetic stays exact where floating-point rupees would not.

vectors.name: grouping-divergence-boundary-99999-vs-100000
vectors.proves: QUESTION: at what magnitude do Indian and Western digit grouping first differ? ANSWER: 1,00,000. Below it they are identical, which is why every five-digit figure in this project is structurally blind to a locale bug (DC-002).

vectors.name: six-digit-supplier-outstanding
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does a shop owing 1,50,000 to suppliers compute correctly? ANSWER: yes, and it is the smallest realistic figure that would expose a Western-grouping bug.

vectors.name: seven-digit-amounts-stay-exact-and-group-correctly
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does the adversarial shop figure of 12,45,600 survive the engine and the render boundary? ANSWER: yes - integer paise are exact at this magnitude.

vectors.name: bi6-single-customer-holds-everything
vectors.proves: QUESTION: what does concentration report when ONE customer owes the entire udhar book? ANSWER: 10000 bp - the worst case the metric exists to surface.

vectors.name: bi6-two-customers-top-three-is-the-whole-book
vectors.proves: QUESTION: what does the top-THREE share report when the shop has only two customers? ANSWER: 10000 bp. A two-customer book genuinely is fully concentrated.

vectors.name: collection-takes-an-outstanding-to-exactly-zero
vectors.proves: QUESTION: can a collection settle a customer to exactly zero without going negative or leaving a rounding tail? ANSWER: yes - integer paise settle exactly.

vectors.name: eight-sections-skipped-one-entry
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does a day with a single entry and everything else deliberately skipped reach ready? ANSWER: yes - a skip is a decision, so all 8 sections are resolved.

vectors.name: forty-entries-in-one-section
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does a busy section sum exactly over many entries? ANSWER: yes. Forty cash sales of 37.77 sum to 1,510.80 with no floating-point drift.

vectors.name: year-boundary-aging-and-horizon
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does date arithmetic survive a YEAR boundary? ANSWER: yes. Every other vector computes 2026-07-15; nothing crossed 31 December until this one (F-03).

vectors.name: leap-day-arithmetic
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does 29 February exist for the aging maths? ANSWER: yes. 2024-01-30 to 2024-02-29 is exactly 30 days, which sits on the aging threshold (F-03).

vectors.name: imported-source-participates-identically
vectors.proves: QUESTION: does an entry with source "imported" behave exactly like a manual one? ANSWER: yes. That column exists so D1 stays reversible, and until now NO fixture had ever set it to anything but manual (F-04).

vectors.name: expense-labels-are-carried
vectors.proves: QUESTION: do labelled expenses total correctly? ANSWER: yes. No fixture populated the label field at all before this - the Form C description column (F-09).

vectors.name: format-paise-uses-indian-grouping-and-latin-numerals
vectors.proves: The render boundary groups 1,23,456.78 the Indian way, always in Latin numerals, in every language. Hand-rolled rather than Intl, so Hermes and Node agree.

vectors.name: day-state-ready-when-all-sections-done
vectors.proves: The day walks to ready when the eighth section is entered or skipped.

vectors.name: day-state-closed-is-terminal
vectors.proves: A closed day stays closed regardless of what is derived beneath it.
